stem: A primary care practice adopts a patient-centered medical home model. Which description best reflects this model?

options.A: Care is organized mainly around isolated acute visits with limited responsibility for coordination across clinicians, settings, or periods between appointments.
options.B: Care decisions are directed primarily by clinicians without incorporating patient preferences because standardization takes priority over individualized goals.
options.C: Care is comprehensive, patient-centered, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety within an ongoing primary care model.
options.D: Care is delivered only during inpatient admissions because the medical-home model is designed for hospital-based management rather than longitudinal primary care.

rationale: AHRQ defines the patient-centered medical home as a model for organizing primary care around five core functions: comprehensive care, patient-centered care, coordinated care, accessible services, and quality and safety. C includes all five defining attributes. A describes fragmented episodic care, B excludes the patient-centered partnership central to the model, and D incorrectly limits the model to inpatient care.
educational_objective: Identify the five core functions of the patient-centered medical home: comprehensive, patient-centered, coordinated, accessible care with a focus on quality and safety.

source_original.stem: A primary care practice adopts a patient-centered medical home model. Which description best reflects this model?

options.A: Care is organized mainly around isolated acute visits, with limited responsibility for coordination across clinicians, settings, or periods between appointments.
options.B: Care decisions are directed primarily by clinicians without incorporating patient preferences, because standardization takes priority over individualized goals.
options.C: Care is comprehensive, patient-centered, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety, usually through an ongoing team-based primary care approach.
options.D: Care is delivered only during inpatient admissions, because the medical-home model is designed for hospital-based management rather than longitudinal primary care.

source_original.rationale: AHRQ defines the patient-centered medical home as comprehensive, patient-centered, coordinated, accessible, and focused on quality and safety, with team-based care supporting those functions. Option C includes these defining attributes. Option A reduces the model to disconnected episodic care. Option B removes patient preferences from decision-making. Option D incorrectly limits the medical-home model to inpatient care rather than longitudinal primary care.
source_original.source_detail: AHRQ — Defining the Patient-Centered Medical Home: five core attributes are comprehensive care, patient-centered care, coordinated care, accessible services, and quality and safety, typically supported by team-based primary care.
